headline: Market turmoil: Prices of fish, eggs, and vegetables surge in Dhaka
summary: Rising fuel costs and supply shortages have driven up the prices of essential commodities, leaving low-income consumers struggling.
details: The prices of fish, eggs, and various vegetables have surged in Dhaka's markets, causing significant distress to consumers. The hike is attributed to fuel price increases and supply shortages.

Cultivated Rui and Katla fish prices have risen by over 50 Taka per kg, while some river fish are now up to 200 Taka more per kg than last week. This is partly due to the ban on Hilsa fishing, which has reduced the overall supply of other marine fish.
The poultry market remains high, with native chickens costing 600 Taka per kg and broiler chickens at 190 Taka per kg. Sellers blame the increase in poultry feed costs for these high prices.
Beef remains steady at 780 to 800 Taka per kg, while mutton has seen a slight decrease of 100 Taka, now selling for 1,200 Taka per kg.
Egg prices remain high, with red eggs selling for 150 Taka per dozen and white eggs for 140 Taka per dozen in major markets, with prices often higher in local neighborhood shops.
Winter vegetables have begun to arrive in the market, but prices for cauliflower and bitter gourd have increased. Prices for beans, tomatoes, and coriander leaves have also spiked significantly.
Sellers claim that prices may stabilize as more seasonal shipments arrive, though they note that increased production costs mean farmers are not seeing the full benefit of the higher retail prices.
caption:
From fish to eggs and vegetables, essential food prices are skyrocketing in Dhaka. Consumers are facing a new wave of price hikes.

The prices of fish, eggs, and various vegetables have surged in Dhaka's markets, causing significant distress to consumers. The hike is attributed to fuel price increases and supply shortages.

Cultivated Rui and Katla fish prices have risen by over 50 Taka per kg, while some river fish are now up to 200 Taka more per kg than last week. This is partly due to the ban on Hilsa fishing, which has reduced the overall supply of other marine fish.

The poultry market remains high, with native chickens costing 600 Taka per kg and broiler chickens at 190 Taka per kg. Sellers blame the increase in poultry feed costs for these high prices.

Beef remains steady at 780 to 800 Taka per kg, while mutton has seen a slight decrease of 100 Taka, now selling for 1,200 Taka per kg.

Egg prices remain high, with red eggs selling for 150 Taka per dozen and white eggs for 140 Taka per dozen in major markets, with prices often higher in local neighborhood shops.

Winter vegetables have begun to arrive in the market, but prices for cauliflower and bitter gourd have increased. Prices for beans, tomatoes, and coriander leaves have also spiked significantly.

Sellers claim that prices may stabilize as more seasonal shipments arrive, though they note that increased production costs mean farmers are not seeing the full benefit of the higher retail prices.

headline: Friday morning: Dhaka air 5th worst in world
summary: The capital city's air quality index has plummeted, placing it among the top five most polluted cities globally on Friday morning.
details: Dhaka's air quality reached critical levels on Friday morning, ranking as the 5th worst in the world.
The city continues to struggle with severe pollution, frequently appearing on global air quality indices.
High levels of particulate matter in the air pose significant health risks to residents and commuters.
Authorities and environmentalists continue to call for stricter pollution controls to combat the smog that often blankets the city.
caption:
